title: Thrift: Allow partial definition of sub-dissectors
description:
When written by hand, it’s difficult to have a fully functional
subdissector for a given command if the structures in it contain at lot
of fields and/or numerous level of sub-structures, making the definition
of all sub-structures mandatory before we have all sub-structures fully
defined before we can dissect anything.

This patch makes it easy not to defined some structure fields and let
the generic Thrift dissector handle them.

If you care only about some fields for your analysis or you have some
obsolete fields that may appear in your captures due to old client but
are no longer defined in the .thrift files, you can still write the
sub-dissector for your protocol just by omitting the obsolete field.

For example:
```c
static const thrift_member_t tcustom_data[] = {
    { &hf_tcustom_data_id, 1, TRUE, DE_THRIFT_T_I64, TMFILL },
    { &hf_tcustom_data_name, 2, TRUE, DE_THRIFT_T_BINARY, TMUTF8 },
    { &hf_tcustom_data_content, 3, TRUE, DE_THRIFT_T_STRUCT, &ett_tcustom_resource, { .members = tcustom_resource } },
    { NULL, 0, FALSE, DE_THRIFT_T_STOP, TMFILL }
};
```

could become:

```c
static const thrift_member_t tcustom_data[] = {
    { &hf_tcustom_data_id, 1, TRUE, DE_THRIFT_T_I64, TMFILL },
    { &hf_tcustom_data_name, 2, TRUE, DE_THRIFT_T_BINARY, TMUTF8 },
    { NULL, 3, TRUE, DE_THRIFT_T_GENERIC, TMUTF8 },
    { NULL, 0, FALSE, DE_THRIFT_T_STOP, TMFILL }
};
```

and avoid the need to define the extremely complex "resource" struct.

In this case, the structured data would be dissected by the generic
dissector while keeping the possibility for the user to filter on
the resource id or name.

*Edit*: This change relies on the fact that structure fields are always order numerically on the network.

* If the found field id is smaller than the next expected one, it means that the user did not provide a definition for it so we switch to generic dissection.
* If the found field id is greater than the next expected one, it means that the field is missing so we continue with the optional/required check.
* Plus additional checks to properly handle the case were the last fields of the structure are the ones that are not specified by the sub-dissector.

> This change relies on the fact that structure fields are always order numerically on the network.

This makes it less desirable to include, IMHO. Reason is that Wireshark especially is called into action when there's trouble in the communications, there's a lot of emphasis on handling _incorrect_ network data. Changing the dissector to make it less resistant against network protocol errors I find undesirable.

I do see your point and I agree with the necessity to keep dissector resistant to errors.

However, I don’t think that change makes the dissector less resistant to errors (I would even go to say it’s more resistant to the issue).

The caller (the sub-dissector) have absolutely no choice but to rely on this fact as there is no way to handle unordered fields.

Before the change, if the field were incorrectly ordered, the dissector would have fail even if this is not necessarily an issue on the application side (I’ll try to forge a request with unordered fields to see how an application might react if you think it will help take a decision).

If we consider a case where field 2 appears after field 3 on the network:

* If field 2 was mandatory, it fails in exactly the same way (when finding field 3 instead of 2).
* If field 2 was optional, it also fails in the same way (when finding field 2 instead of 4).

The only case were the unordered fields might go undetected is when it happens after _all_ the defined mandatory fields are dissected.
I can add an additional check indicating that fields are unordered but in this case it should probably also be in the generic dissector without any specific sub-dissector (as a warning only because it can be well-formed).

Proposal:
1. Update this MR to add a warning when we fallback to the generic dissector (it also helps tracking what is not handled yet so I don’t see any downside to this part). **Edit**: Done.
2. Create a new MR to detect the unordered fields both in generic and specific sub-dissectors. **Edit**: Done in !4113

Would it be acceptable as we are able to continue with the dissection but see the issue?

Hello @JaapKeuter, I believe that Anders’ proposal (which is now implemented) addresses your concerns so I’m marking this thread as resolved.

Do not hesitate if you think there is anything else.

Hi,
How about having DE_THRIFT_FLD_ONLY or DE_GENERIC or something as an decoding option? In that way
it should be clear that field 3 from your example is expected but it will only have the thrift fields
decoded.
Best regards
Anders

Nice idea, and as long as I keep the value out of the {0..15} range, there is no risk of conflict with Thrift values (-1 seems right for this kind of use).

I’ll see what I can cook, thanks for the proposal.

Hello @AndersBroman, I updated the description (the second code block) from what I understood and will proceed for the matching implementation.

Please tell if it’s any different from what you had in mind.

Also, what do you think about the associated expert info? Maybe I can lower it to `PI_NOTE` as the user explicitly requested the delegation.

Now implemented, so I mark this thread as resolved as well.

Note: the `guint32` to `gint32` is a fix for a signedness comparison warning that was not seen previously (holding types so 0 to 15 anyway).
